name: Coats plus syndrome
aliases: Cerebroretinal microangiopathy with calcifications and cysts

reference.source: Telomere biology disorder and neurogenetics references
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive telomere biology disorder, also known as cerebroretinal microangiopathy with calcifications and cysts (CRMCC).
Most cases result from biallelic CTC1 variants (a component of the CST/CTC1-STN1-TEN1 telomere-replication complex); some are due to STN1 (OBFC1), and a POT1-related phenocopy is recognised.
The ophthalmological hallmark is bilateral exudative (Coats disease-like) retinopathy with retinal telangiectasia and a risk of detachment.

Neurological features include intracranial calcification (basal ganglia, thalami and deep white matter), leucoencephalopathy and parenchymal brain cysts, causing seizures, spasticity, dystonia and cognitive decline.
Systemic vascular fragility manifests as gastrointestinal bleeding from vascular ectasia, portal hypertension, osteopenia with fractures and poor bone healing, and anaemia.
Intrauterine growth restriction and prenatal onset can occur.

It must be distinguished from Labrune syndrome (leukoencephalopathy with calcifications and cysts, due to SNORD118), which is confined to the central nervous system without retinal or systemic features.
reference.pathophysiology: Coats plus (CRMCC) is a telomere biology disorder caused predominantly by biallelic loss-of-function variants in CTC1, which encodes conserved telomere capping component 1, a subunit of the CST complex (CTC1-STN1-TEN1). CST cooperates with DNA polymerase alpha-primase to complete replication of the telomeric C-strand and to restart stalled replication forks; impaired CST function leads to defective telomere replication, telomere shortening and fragility, and genomic instability. The clinical picture is dominated by a small-vessel angiopathy: retinal telangiectasia with exudation (a Coats-type retinopathy), a cerebral microangiopathy producing calcification, leucoencephalopathy and cyst formation, and systemic vascular ectasia causing gastrointestinal haemorrhage and portal hypertension, together with osteopenia. Rare cases arise from STN1 variants, and there is phenotypic overlap with POT1-related disease, placing the condition firmly within the telomeropathy spectrum and distinct from SNORD118-related Labrune syndrome, which lacks extraneurological involvement.
additionalDifferentials: Labrune syndrome / leukoencephalopathy with calcifications and cysts (SNORD118) — central-nervous-system-limited
Coats disease (isolated, usually unilateral exudative retinopathy)
Revesz syndrome (TINF2) and other telomere biology disorders
additionalInvestigations: CTC1 sequencing, with STN1 and POT1 or a broader telomere-gene panel if negative
Brain CT and MRI for calcification, leucoencephalopathy and cysts
Full blood count and iron studies with investigation of gastrointestinal bleeding (endoscopy)
Bone imaging and assessment for osteopenia and fractures
redFlags: Enlarging intracranial cysts causing mass effect or raised intracranial pressure
Progressive cytopenias or a bleeding tendency
Pathological fractures or poor bone healing
reference.prognosis: Progressive and variable; neurological deterioration, recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding and complications of brain cysts limit life expectancy, although some milder cases survive into adulthood.
pitfalls: Confusing Coats plus with Labrune syndrome — the retinal, gastrointestinal and skeletal features and the CTC1 genotype distinguish it
Diagnosing isolated Coats disease and missing the multisystem CRMCC picture
Underestimating bleeding risk from gastrointestinal vascular ectasia before invasive procedures
Over-reliance on telomere length, which may not be uniformly short in all CST-related cases
Missing the autosomal recessive inheritance and the resulting sibling recurrence risk
references: Inherited bone marrow failure syndrome guidelines
management: Ophthalmic treatment of the Coats-like exudative retinopathy with laser photocoagulation, cryotherapy or anti-VEGF injections to preserve vision.
Neurological management of seizures with antiseizure medication and of spasticity and dystonia, with neurosurgical intervention for symptomatic enlarging brain cysts.
Endoscopic treatment of gastrointestinal vascular ectasia, with iron replacement and transfusion for anaemia and management of portal hypertension.
Management of osteopenia and fragility fractures with attention to poor bone healing.
Nutritional and growth support given intrauterine growth restriction and failure to thrive.
Genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive telomere biology disorder, with testing of at-risk family members.
Multidisciplinary and palliative supportive care coordinating ophthalmology, neurology, gastroenterology and genetics given the progressive course.
